items.stem: Besides the Buddha, who stayed behind in the grove?
items.quote: where Govinda stayed behind
items.why: His friend now walks a different path.

items.stem: What does Siddhartha realize he has turned into?
items.quote: He realized that he was no youth any more, but had turned into a man.
items.why: His youth is behind him.

items.stem: When Siddhartha opens his eyes, what fills his face?
items.quote: Siddhartha opened his eyes and looked around, a smile filled his face
items.why: A new lightness comes over him.

items.stem: Which colours does Siddhartha notice in the world?
items.quote: Here was blue, here was yellow, here was green
items.why: He sees colour as if for the first time.

items.stem: After his realization, Siddhartha walks on quickly.
items.quote: walked quickly like a man who knows what he has got to do.
items.why: He moves with new purpose.

items.stem: The world now looks dull and grey to Siddhartha.
items.quote: Beautiful was the world, colourful was the world
items.why: He finds the world beautiful and colourful.

items.stem: Complete: “walked quickly like a man who knows what he has got to ____.”
items.quote: walked quickly like a man who knows what he has got to do.
items.why: He walks like someone sure of his task.

items.stem: Complete: “How deaf and ____ have I been!”
items.quote: “How deaf and stupid have I been!”
items.why: He scolds himself for his past blindness.

items.stem: Match each part of the scene to what it does.
items.why: Each detail of the scene is alive to him now.
evidence: the sky and the river flowed
the forest and the mountains were rigid
in its midst was he, Siddhartha, the awakening one

items.stem: Put these events in story order.
items.why: His walk from the grove is a walk into new thoughts.

cards.text: He realizes he is now a man
He stops, gripped by a thought

evidence: When Siddhartha left the grove
He realized that he was no youth any more
he now stopped as these thoughts caught hold of him
Siddhartha opened his eyes and looked around

items.stem: To what does the narrator compare Siddhartha's deep pondering?
items.quote: He pondered deeply, like diving into a deep water
items.why: He sinks down into his feeling to find its causes.

items.stem: What wish has left Siddhartha, like a snake's old skin?
items.quote: the wish to have teachers and to listen to teachings
items.why: He no longer looks for a master.

items.stem: What does Siddhartha say he knows least about?
items.quote: And there is no thing in this world I know less about than about me, about Siddhartha!
items.why: His own self is his greatest mystery.

items.stem: What did Siddhartha try to peel off to find the Atman?
items.quote: I was willing to dissect my self and peel off all of its layers
items.why: He tried to reach the core by stripping himself away.

items.stem: Siddhartha looks around as if seeing the world for the first time.
items.quote: He looked around, as if he was seeing the world for the first time.
items.why: Everything looks new to him.

items.stem: Siddhartha says he managed to overcome his self.
items.quote: But I was not able to overcome it, could only deceive it, could only flee from it, only hide from it.
items.why: He could only flee or hide from it.

items.stem: Complete: “I was afraid of myself, I was ____ from myself!”
items.quote: I was afraid of myself, I was fleeing from myself!
items.why: He names how he treated his own self.

items.stem: Match each image to what it stands for.
items.why: Images make his inner change visible.
evidence: as a snake is left by its old skin
a feeling of awakening from long dreams
I do not want to kill and dissect myself any longer, to find a secret behind the ruins.

items.stem: Put Siddhartha's resolutions in ¶6 in order.
items.why: His vows build to learning from himself.
evidence: now I would not let Siddhartha escape from me again!
No longer, I want to begin my thoughts and my life with Atman
I do not want to kill and dissect myself any longer
want to be my student

items.stem: Put these moments in order.
items.why: Joy at the world turns to a sudden halt, then firmness.

cards.text: He stops as if at a snake
He calls himself deaf and stupid

evidence: He looked around, as if he was seeing the world for the first time.
“How deaf and stupid have I been!”
Siddhartha stopped once again, suddenly
Siddhartha emerged, more a self than before

items.stem: Fleeing himself, what did Siddhartha search for instead?
items.quote: I searched Atman, I searched Brahman
items.why: He looked everywhere except at himself.

items.stem: Why does Siddhartha seek the causes of his feeling?
items.quote: by this alone sensations turn into realizations and are not lost
items.why: Finding causes turns feelings into lasting insight.

items.stem: Why did Siddhartha have to part with the Buddha?
items.quote: had to part with him, was not able to accept his teachings.
items.why: He honours the Buddha but cannot follow a teaching.

items.stem: Why does Siddhartha walk quickly in ¶5?
items.quote: walked quickly like a man who knows what he has got to do.
items.why: Purpose, not fear, sets his pace.

items.stem: Soon after the moment, Siddhartha walks on swiftly and impatiently.
items.quote: started to proceed swiftly and impatiently
items.why: The shock leaves him eager to move on.

items.stem: Siddhartha leaves the Buddha because he dislikes him.
items.quote: the highest and wisest teacher, the most holy one, Buddha
items.why: He reveres the Buddha; he cannot accept a teaching.

items.stem: Complete: “so it seemed to him, is the very essence of ____”
items.quote: so it seemed to him, is the very essence of thinking
items.why: This belief shapes how he handles his feelings.

items.stem: Complete: “But I have lost ____ in the process.”
items.quote: But I have lost myself in the process.
items.why: Searching for Atman cost him his own self.

items.stem: Match each moment to what it leads to.
items.why: Each inner moment produces an outward change.
evidence: he now stopped as these thoughts caught hold of him
a smile filled his face and a feeling of awakening from long dreams flowed through him
Beautiful was the world

items.stem: Order the steps of Siddhartha's self-questioning.
items.why: Each answer leads to a deeper question.

cards.text: Finds he was afraid of himself
Admits he could only flee it

evidence: what they, who have taught you much, were still unable to teach you?
It was the self, the purpose and essence of which I sought to learn.
could only flee from it
I was afraid of myself

items.stem: In ¶8, what did Siddhartha call his eyes and his tongue?
items.quote: called my eyes and my tongue coincidental and worthless forms without substance
items.why: He once scorned his own senses.

items.stem: Sensations “start to emit like rays of light what is inside of them.” What does this image suggest?
items.quote: start to emit like rays of light what is inside of them.
items.why: Understood feelings give off meaning.

items.stem: “this mystery of me being alive, of me being one and being separated” points to what theme?
items.quote: this mystery of me being alive, of me being one and being separated and isolated from all others
items.why: His central question is the self.

items.stem: What does “Blue was blue, river was river” chiefly convey?
items.quote: Blue was blue, river was river
items.why: He accepts things as they appear.

items.stem: What does “taking a deep breath” before his vows suggest?
items.quote: “Oh,” he thought, taking a deep breath
items.why: He gathers himself to begin anew.

items.stem: The repeated “It was the self … It was the self” mainly stresses what?
items.quote: It was the self, I wanted to free myself from
items.why: All his searching had one object.

items.stem: The list of colours in ¶7 shows his senses waking to the world.
items.quote: Here was blue, here was yellow, here was green
items.why: The colours mark his new seeing.

items.stem: Siddhartha decides only the hidden meaning behind things deserves attention.
items.quote: he will not scorn the symbols and letters
items.why: He now values the surface too.

items.stem: Complete: “This had been the last ____ of the awakening”
items.quote: This had been the last tremor of the awakening
items.why: The image ties his awakening to a birth's final pangs.

items.stem: Order the steps of his reasoning in ¶7-8.
items.why: Delight leads to a judgement on his past.

cards.text: I have been deaf and stupid

evidence: Beautiful was the world
Blue was blue
How deaf and stupid have I been
have not been born before this very day
